hypothesis: A sorted sparse-obstacle path-counting method can avoid the quadratic grid scan when its pairwise work is clearly lower, while a contiguous one-row DP fallback reduces memory use and improves locality for denser cases.
notes: No speedup is established by the supplied observations; correctness and performance remain for the controller to evaluate.
transformations: Replace the N-by-N blocked grid and two-row DP with sorted, deduplicated obstacle coordinates and a contiguous one-row, row-major DP fallback.
For sparse obstacles, use factorial-based binomial path counts with inclusion-exclusion over prior reachable obstacles; explicitly handle blocked endpoints and N=1.
Select the pairwise method only when its estimated work is at most 1/1024 of the dense cell count; use conditional modular subtraction in the dense recurrence instead of remainder division.
